timeline.body:
Always update the monitoring templates using the `getIndexTemplateMetadataUpgrader` 
infrastructure.

Previously the `LocalExporter` was responsible for upgrading the monitoring templates, however
the local exporter could be disabled (or the first bulk to resolve that would trigger the upgrade could
arrive at non-deterministic times).

This removes the template upgrading from the `LocalExporter` and moves them to
the `getIndexTemplateMetadataUpgrader` infrastructure.

Fixes #82453

timeline.body: the APM template(s) are separate from the monitoring templates. Can you move this out of the monitoring code (likely a different PR) ?

reply.body:
I wouldn't know where to place them as we don't install and manage the APM stuff (it's APM that installs these templates AFAIK). So, if we are to take advantage of our generic Plugin infrastructure to delete these templates we'd need a new Plugin (APMPlugin?) just to do this or otherwise, we'd need code the removal of APM templates somewhere _else_ that again doesn't know of APM.

Based on the above and the fact the APM is a form of monitoring I thought it's alright to have the cleanup as part of the Monitoring plugin. 

Am I missing something? Is there a better place in Elasticsearch to manage them?

> Am I missing something? 

nope

not sure ... i guess this makes sense if there is no other place, although it probably needs a comment to the effect.

reply.body: Yes. In case `Monitoring.loadTemplate` throws some generic `IllegalArgumentException` (ie. in case an invalid ID is passed in, or the underlying resource file is not found)
Can you catch the more specific exception ?

So this is a bit of paranoia driven development. Any exception that leaks this method would cause a node to not start. There's a `String.format` inside the `loadTemplate` method so we'd need to catch `IllegalFormatException` and `IllegalArgumentException` - and if `loadTemplate` changes or yields a famous NPE somewhere we'd be exposed again. 

Would it be alright to keep this as is and add a comment explaining why we're catching everything?
I'll defer that question to @dakrone and/or @jbaiera

I think a comment would be good. I'm usually very against leaking exceptions that could kill a node outright if they aren't `Error`s. In this case we're trying to upgrade some templates. I don't think this is so critical to cluster health that we should sink a node at startup if the process fails for some reason.

+===== `must_not` clauses and `nested` queries
+
+If a `nested` query matches one or more nested objects in a document, it returns
+the document as a hit. This applies even if other nested objects in the document
+don't match the query. Keep this in mind when using a `nested` query that
+contains an inner <<query-dsl-bool-query,`must_not` clause>>.
+
+TIP: Use the <<inner-hits,`inner_hits`>> parameter to see which nested objects
+matched a `nested` query.
+
+For example, the following search uses an outer `nested` query with an inner
+`must_not` clause.
+
+[source,console]
+----
+PUT my-index
+{
+  "mappings": {
+    "properties": {
+      "comments": {
+        "type": "nested"
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}

+      "author": "kimchy"
+    }
+  ]

+    }
